checks: No eclipse at 1 of 3 covered epochs where the 7.95668 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 80518171 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 7.9567 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse shows a dimming of 16.70%, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 5.5 sigma significance. The Box Least Squares detection achieved a signal-to-noise ratio of 78.8, and pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 82.9, though the centroid offset of 3.1 arcseconds from the target position warrants consideration. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it potentially novel. The machine learning screening score of 0.44 indicates moderate confidence in the pipeline's assessment of this as a genuine target star, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
